entries.title: Bears' handoff to G Joe Thuney on trick play disallowed
entries.summary: <p>The Bears were flagged for an illegal forward handoff on a trick play in the second quarter of Thursday night's game against the Patriots at Soldier Field.</p><p>The Bears put tight end Colston Loveland at left tackle and had left tackle Ozzy Trapilo line up to the right of their right tackle. Caleb Williams took the snap and handed the ball forward to left guard Joe Thuney, who ran for four yards.</p><p>Thuney, a former Patriots legend, was flagged because it’s illegal to hand the ball forward to an interior lineman.</p><p>The Bears were forced to kick a field goal after receiver Rome Odunze was flagged for offensive pass interference on the next play. </p><h3>Notes</h3><p>• Linebacker T.J. Edwards, who was listed as doubtful because of a hamstring injury Wednesday, was inactive.</p><p>• Cubs star Pete Crow-Amstrong and White Sox second baseman Chase Meidroth chatted on the field before the game.</p><p>• Patriots Pro Bowl cornerback Christian Gonzalez was downgraded to questionable with an illness before kickoff, but played.<br></p>
entries.author: Patrick Finley

entries.title: Halftime: Bears lead Patriots 20-14 after wild ending to first half
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> are up 20-14 on the Patriots at halftime Thursday thanks mainly to some big plays by wide receiver Luther Burden and a timely interception by linebacker D'Marco Jackson.</p><p>They had a chance to go into halftime up 20-7 and getting the ball to begin the third quarter, but squandered that with a sloppy final play. With three seconds left, Patriots quarterback Drake Maye dumped the ball off to running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who ran to the end zone for a 48-yard touchdown.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="fr" dir="ltr">RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️<br><br>📺 Prime Video <a href="https://t.co/heXDiTFnzW">pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW</a></p>— New England Patriots (@Patriots) <a href="https://x.com/Patriots/status/2113446816603570284?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 23, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Burden is at 130 yards and a touchdown on just four catches, and quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/01/money-isnt-everything-with-a-big-contract-in-reach-qb-caleb-williams-wants-to-make-sure-bears-keep-winning" >Caleb Williams</a> has completed 9 of 16 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown for a 113.3 passer rating.</p><p>Jackson ended the Patriots' best threat at scoring touchdown by picking off a pass from Drake Maye in the end zone. </p><p>The Bears jumped to a 10-0 lead by overwhelming the Patriots on both sides of the ball.</p><p>The Patriots’ opening drive ended on fourth-and-five at the Bears’ 45-yard line when nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon — Who else? — blitzed to sack Drake Maye. Gordon had three sacks Sunday against the Falcons in his season debut and leads all NFL defensive backs for the season.</p><p>Williams followed immediately with a 26-yard pass to Luther Burden to put the Bears in scoring position, and they eventually settled for a 43-yard field goal by Cairo Santos. He and Burden struck again on a 58-yard pass late in the first quarter to set up D’Andre Swift’s four-yard touchdown run.</p><p>The Bears had a chance to run away with the game when Williams hit Burden on a 24-yard screen pass for a touchdown and a 20-7 lead with 14 seconds left in the first half, but had an incomprehensible defensive lapse.</p><p>Maye hit A.J. Brown for 18 yards, then called timeout at the Bears’ 48-yard line with three seconds left. The Bears were in prevent defense with safeties Dillon Thieneman and Skyler Thomas at the goal line, and Maye threw underneath, seemingly harmlessly, to Stevenson.</p><p>The Bears had five players between Stevenson and the end zone at the time he caught the pass, plus defensive back Cam Lewis chasing him from behind, but he weaved through them all the way down the field for a touchdown.</p><p>The Bears get the ball to begin the second half.</p><p>Here are the Bears' inactives for the game:</p><p>QB Case Keenum*<br>RB Kyle Monangai (thumb, toe)<br>OL Jordan McFadden</p><p>DL Jayden Loving<br>LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring)<br>LB Jack Sanborn (concussion)<br>CB Nick McCloud</p><p>* - designated as emergency third quarterback</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears pay tribute to Mike Ditka on 'Thursday Night Football'
entries.summary: <p>There’s been no plan made for a public memorial for Mike Ditka.</p><p>Thursday night, then, might have to suffice.</p><p>Playing their first home game since the man synonymous with their franchise died Oct. 9, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> paid tribute to the legendary coach and Pro Football Hall of Fame player at Soldier Field.</p><p>The Bears handed out fake mustaches to all fans and a headband in the style of Ditka's trademark sweater vest to the first 10,000. They held a moment of silence before playing the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-patriots-mike-ditka-pay-tribute-head-coach-player-89-number" target="_blank" >Patriots</a>, the same team Ditka beat in Super Bowl XX.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="113" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/3a0znM7xEA0?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Bears hold moment of silence for Mike Ditka"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>"If it wasn't for Ditka, we wouldn't have the Super Bowl," former center Jay Hilgenberg said in an on-field interview aired on the scoreboard.</p><p>The Bears stenciled a football with Ditka's No. 89 on it onto the northwest sideline. They wore a matching patch over the hearts of their jerseys.</p><p>Chairman George McCaskey wore a navy Ditka jersey over his French blue dress shirt. Bears guard Jonah Jackson walked into the stadium wearing a white long-sleeved No. 89 jersey.</p><p>Ditka's number was the last one retired by the Bears.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="113" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/wDOhJ7_sET4?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Bears fans get Mike Ditka mustaches at Soldier Field"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>Tom Borich and his 12-year-old grandson, Kieran Chucketts, both from Superior, Wis., came to pay their respects.</p><p>"I've been a Bears fan since the 1960s, but I was always by myself in the land of Packers and Vikings fans — until my son-in-law and grandson came into the picture,” Borich said. “Now I've finally got some Bears fans to root with me. It's been a wonderful time.</p><p>“Ditka embodies the toughness of Chicago and the toughness of the Bears. We're excited to be here."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/jonahjackson73?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@jonahjackson73</a> reppin' Da Coach 🤝 <a href="https://t.co/7WjFZBbV1u">pic.twitter.com/7WjFZBbV1u</a></p>— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) <a href="https://x.com/ChicagoBears/status/2113379171120386551?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 22, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Ditka’s Pro Football Hall of Fame display on the south concourse showed off a sweater vest and gold jacket. Ditka, who had 4,503 receiving yards from 1961-66, was the first tight end ever inducted into the Hall.</p><p>A private funeral for Ditka has already taken place.</p><p><i>Ashlee Rezin contributed.</i></p>

entries.title: CPS approves $300,000 for family of girl who endured years of racist bullying
entries.summary: <p>The mother of a Black student who endured racist bullying for more than two years at a predominantly white Northwest Side elementary school is set to receive a $300,000 settlement from Chicago Public Schools.</p><p>The city’s Board of Education unanimously voted to approve the payment at its monthly meeting Thursday, more than a year after the Chicago Sun-Times and WBEZ published an <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/education/2025/06/13/black-girl-endured-racist-bullying-mostly-white-chicago-school-cps" target="_blank" ><u>investigation into the incessant bullying and failures</u></a> by the school administration to curb it.</p><p>The student’s mother, Sher’Ron Hinton, filed a lawsuit against the district in July 2025 accusing the staff at Wildwood IB World Magnet School of “willful and wanton conduct” and negligence for allowing her daughter to be subjected to “extreme acts of race-based bullying, sexual harassment and sexual abuse.”</p><p>Hundreds of pages of school incident reports filled out by Wildwood staff and emails from educators showed the girl, who the Sun-Times and WBEZ called Jada to protect her identity, was subjected to repeated racial slurs, body-shaming, encouragement to kill herself and, in one case, touching “in places I don’t want to be touched.”</p><p>She told school employees four times in fifth grade that she had suicidal thoughts.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-f40000" entries.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson considers TE Cole Kmet's right knee injury serious
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> tight end Cole Kmet was carted off the field in the fourth quarter Thursday night after hurting his right knee.</p><p>Kmet caught a second-down pass from quarterback Caleb Williams and ran up the Bears' sideline, where he was tackled. Kmet went down immediately, was surrounded by teammates and coaches and was eventually taken to the locker room.</p><p>The tight end was cheered as he was carted into the northwest tunnel. He gave a thumbs up to fans.</p><p>The Bears ruled him out shortly, and coach Ben Johnson was grim about the outlook afterward.</p><p>“I don’t think it looked very good," he said.</p><p>For a coach who rarely reveals much about injuries, that’s his way of saying that was a serious one.</p><p>Kmet had three catches for 28 yards against the Patriots. The catch on which was injured was a big moment for the Bears, who held a six-point lead and were facing second-and-nine from their own 10-yard line. </p><p>Kmet, a second-round pick out of Notre Dame in 2020, is the Bears' most senior offensive player. He entered the game with seven catches for 59 yards on the season.<br></p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears K Cairo Santos 'annoyed' by miss even after booting career-long FG
entries.summary: <p>Cairo Santos wasn’t smiling in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ locker room even after hitting a career-long 58-yard field goal Thursday night to salt away the Bears’ 30-24 win against the Patriots.</p><p>He was still "annoyed" with himself after hitting the left upright on a 53-yard try earlier in the fourth quarter that would have put the Bears ahead by nine. Santos has missed a field goal in each of his last three games — a 43-yarder wide left against the Packers and a 56-yarder wide left against the Falcons.</p><p>“I’m having a hard time celebrating these moments,” he said. “I shouldn’t act this way. But I just feel lieke I’m hitting the ball way too good to have these misses happen. Even though they’re from 50-plus, I’ve been making them all the time.”</p><p>Santos said he hit the left upright because he was trying to play a draw.</p><p>Quarterback Caleb Williams had taken a sack on third-and-five from the Patriots’ 30 with 1:39 to play. New England defensive lineman Christian Barmore was hurt on the play. Johnson had wanted to punt, but talked to special teams coordinator Richard Hightower during the injury timeout.</p><p>He asked if Santos wanted to kick the 58-yarder. Santos had already told his position coach that he did. Kicking into the south end zone, Santos had made 60-yard kicks during warmups.</p><p>"Just thankful I got the opportunity to bounce back," he said.</p><p></p>

entries.title: Previewing Week 10's top high school football games
entries.summary: <h3><b>Class 8A</b></h3><p><b>Bloom at No. 22 York</b><br><b>6:30 p.m. Friday: </b>After sitting 3-3 at the end of September, York (6-3) now is one of the hottest teams in the state in the wake of consecutive victories against fellow West Suburban Silver powers Downers Grove North, Glenbard West and Lyons by a total of five points. A pair of two-way linemen — Purdue recruit Owen Roberts and Dayton commit Brayden Byford — has led the resurgence. Running back Chris Georgas and quarterback Zack Assaad pace a balanced offense. Bloom (3-6), in the second year of a rebuild under former Simeon coach Dante Culbreath, has a victory against playoff qualifier Champaign Centennial.</p><p><b>Warren at Naperville Central</b><br><b>7 p.m. Friday:</b> After leaning heavily on running back Aaron Stewart — now a freshman wrestler at Illinois — last season, Warren (4-5) is more balanced this fall. Junior Jonathan Randolph has rushed for 1,224 yards and 16 touchdowns, and senior Xavier Vinson has passed for 1,042 yards and 11 touchdowns with five interceptions. Naperville Central (5-4) has won four of its last five games, including 21-17 last week against Neuqua Valley. Simon Hayes threw for 197 yards and three touchdowns, including a pair to DuPage Valley offensive player of the year Mark Williams.</p><p><b>Stevenson at Lockport</b><br><b>7:15 p.m. Friday:</b> Stevenson (4-5) has won four of its last five games after an 0-4 start. Eli Sligal passed for three touchdowns, including a pair to Luke Clark, in a rout last week of Waukegan. Lockport (5-4) was one of the surprises of the postseason last year, reaching the Class 8A semifinals after a 5-4 regular season. The Porters also started slowly this season, losing their first three games. Their only loss since was to No. 1 Lincoln-Way East. Quarterback Griffin Russell has passed for 1,725 yards and 18 touchdowns. His favorite targets are Jaxson Little and Khairi Silas.</p><h3><b>Class 7A</b></h3><p><b>St. Laurence at Belleville East</b><br><b>3 p.m. Saturday:</b> A year after reaching the Class 6A semifinals, St. Laurence (3-6) has been hit hard by injuries and had 18 players sidelined at one point. Illinois-bound linebacker Sean Rice, the Vikings’ best player, just returned last week after hurting his ankle while running through a banner before a game. Belleville East (6-3), which lost its season opener 24-7 against Lincoln-Way West, has won four in a row. Quarterback Kingston Jones has thrown for 1,290 yards and seven touchdowns with five interceptions.</p><h3><b>Class 5A</b></h3><p><b>Mt. Vernon at No. 24 Providence</b><br><b>2 p.m. Saturday: </b>It has been a roller-coaster ride for Providence (6-3). Head coach Tyler Plantz abruptly was fired after the Celtics started 4-0 and were ranked No. 1 in Class 5A. (He’s now a volunteer assistant at Mount Carmel.) They’re 2-3 under interim coach Adam Nissen, including a victory against defending Class 6A champ Fenwick. Running backs Broden Mackert and Brayden McKay and quarterback Dominic Vita all have big-play capability. Mount Vernon (3-6) is on a four-game losing streak, during which it has been outscored 244-100.</p>

entries.title: After Bears' latest win, we can say it: Chicago sports seems to be having a moment
entries.summary: <p>Is Chicago having a sports moment?</p><p>Because with the reigning AFC champion Patriots on the lakefront Thursday for a prime-time game against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> — with the Bears in the role of favorites — it sure felt so.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> just made the playoffs. The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>’ Connor Bedard is back on the ice and skating with Patrick Kane. The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls" target="_blank" >Bulls</a> have rookie Caleb Wilson, who already is proving this town is big enough for two stars with that first name. Start with all that, amplify it with a Bears team that more than occasionally looks good enough to beat any opponent not from the NFC North, throw in Mike Ditka-inspired fake mustaches for as far as the eye can see and what do you have?</p><p>A moment, indeed.</p><p>Every major sports market has its heydays, Chicago included, though the truth is they’ve been few and far between. Boston, for one, has the Patriots coming off a Super Bowl appearance and the Red Sox, Celtics and Bruins all in winning windows, too. Do we have it that good here? Well, maybe we’re getting there.</p><p>The Bears, of course, are the key to the whole operation. If Caleb Williams is spraying the ball around to Luther Burden and Colston Loveland and the team is winning, every game day is a holiday. If the defense is giving up ridiculous Hail Marys and the team is losing, an entire city scowls into its soup. When the Bears are good, man, this place is on fire. But without them leading the way, it’s Sleepy City.</p><p>It was a bit funny to look back at the last time the Bears beat the Patriots at Soldier Field, in 2000. That’s so long ago that Tom Brady was a rookie riding the bench. That December day, the Bears had Shane Matthews at quarterback, James Allen carrying the ball 37 times, passes being caught by guys named Kaseem Sinceno, Scott Dragos and Macey Brooks. Those Bears, bound for a 5-11 finish, had to be one of the most who’s-who of ‘‘who?’’ Bears teams ever, so different from this one right down to the coaches — stoic Dick Jauron vs. incandescent Ben Johnson.</p><p>The Bears went 0-5 against the great Pats teams quarterbacked by Brady, giving up an average of 35 points and losing by an average of just more than 14. On one side, the most successful team in sports. On the other, rarely the cause of much excitement.</p><p>Win or lose, it felt so different this time, and that felt like something. It felt good.</p><p><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></p><p><b>• Caleb Williams Takes Next Step:</b> Maybe some people were too quick to anoint him a superstar, but the quarterback’s play the last two games essentially has been coach Ben Johnson’s dream come true. Be very excited.</p><p><b>• The ‘Problem Child’ Is Exploding: </b>That’s how Williams refers to Luther Burden — as in, the second-year wide receiver is a problem for anybody trying to stop this offense — which is just perfect. What a weapon.</p><p><b>• What’s Wrong With Jaylon Johnson?</b> The cornerback is playing like the weak link of the defense. Can’t cover, can’t tackle, can’t seem to run well. Is he hurt? Is he unmotivated? Answers must come.<b>Williams Takes Next Step: </b>Maybe some people were too quick to anoint him a superstar, but the quarterback’s play the last two games has essentially been Ben Johnson’s dream come true. entries.title: Bears' grades are in. How did they do against the Patriots?
entries.summary: <p>Say this for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-inactives-vs-patriots-lb-t-j-edwards-out-with-hamstring-injury" target="_blank" >a 30-24 win against the Patriots</a> at Soldier Field: Giving Cairo Santos — far from the strongest-legged kicker in the sport — a shot at a 58-yarder to all but put the game away was utterly fearless. Crazy? That, too, but still fearless. It was an A-plus move by Johnson, who would've had a lot of explaining to do had Santos come up short. All's well that ends well.</p><p>Let's get to all the grades:</p><p><b>QUARTERBACK — A-</b></p><p>Caleb Williams became the first Bears quarterback to throw for 300 yards in consecutive games since the great Mitch Trubisky in 2018. He put it where wide receiver Luther Burden could run with it after the catch and fed tight end Colston Loveland as needed. You had to love it when the locked-in Williams gave Burden the business after a 58-yard gain for celebrating instead of getting back to the huddle, requiring a Bears timeout. You also had to be impressed when Williams stood tall, took a big hit and delivered a perfect ball to Loveland — who dropped it — then came right back on the next down with a 22-yard dart to Burden, despite being roughed on the play. A 21-yard completion to Rome Odunze on third-and-11 in the fourth quarter — again under a heavy rush — was Pro Bowl stuff. Williams did take a terrible sack in the final minutes, which potentially could have been very costly, but kicker Cairo Santos took him off the hook.</p><p><b>RUNNING GAME: B</b></p><p>The Bears just don’t have the same oomph without Kyle Monangai, but D’Andre Swift held things down admirably against a tough defense. A tip of the helmet to Swift for not missing any game time after a hard, straight-on hit to his left knee in the first quarter. It tore a big hole in his pants, baring a bloodied knee, but, hey, he’s a hockey player.</p><p><b>TIGHT ENDS: B</b></p><p>Loveland had a second consecutive big game and scored a touchdown, but his pair of drops left some bigger numbers out there. With an early catch, Cole Kmet became only the second Bears tight end to reach the 3,000-receiving-yard mark, joining Mike Ditka. Alas, Kmet appeared to injure his right knee late in the game and had to be carted off.</p><p><b>LINEBACKERS: B-</b></p><p>With T.J. Edwards inactive again, D’Marco Jackson made his presence felt with several hard hits and an interception in the end zone after running step-for-step with tight end Eli Raridon. Otherwise, the linebackers — especially Devin Bush — were flummoxed by the Patriots’ tight ends in coverage. Bush did make a huge third-down, open-field stop on quarterback Drake Maye that forced a punt in the fourth quarter.</p><p><b>DEFENSIVE BACKS: C</b></p><p>The Patriots’ 48-yard touchdown on the final play of the first half — a catch-and-run-run-run by running back Rhamondre Stevenson — involved some colossally bad defense by the guys in the back end. Jaylon Johnson’s effort at a tackle on the play was severely lacking. Yo, Dillon Thieneman? Act like a first-rounder and don’t let that happen.</p><p><b>SPECIAL TEAMS: A-</b></p><p>Santos gave fans the worst kind of 2018 flashbacks when he doinked a 53-yard field-goal attempt with eight minutes left and left the score at 27-21, giving the Patriots a chance to take the lead. But he more than made up for it on a three-field-goal night with a 58-yarder right down the middle to make it 30-21 and all but end the game. Who knew he had 58 in him? Tory Taylor had a 65-yard punt and Zavion Thomas a 47-yard kickoff return. Odunze also fell on the Patriots’ last-gasp onside kick.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="fr" dir="ltr">RHAMONDRE STEVENSON‼️<br><br>📺 Prime Video <a href="https://t.co/heXDiTFnzW">pic.twitter.com/heXDiTFnzW</a></p>— New England Patriots (@Patriots) <a href="https://x.com/Patriots/status/2113446816603570284?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 23, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-inactives-vs-patriots-lb-t-j-edwards-out-with-hamstring-injury" >Bears hang on to beat Patriots 30-24 as Cairo Santos seals victory with career-long 58-yard field goal</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-patriots-cole-kmet-carted-off-with-right-knee-injury" >Bears coach Ben Johnson considers TE Cole Kmet’s right knee injury serious</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-handoff-to-g-joe-thuney-on-trick-play-disallowed" >Bears’ handoff to G Joe Thuney on trick play disallowed</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-patriots-mike-ditka-pay-tribute-head-coach-player-89-number" >Bears pay tribute to Mike Ditka on ‘Thursday Night Football’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
